opinions.reason: I adversarially checked roughly 40 discrete, falsifiable citations across this revised artifact and found none false. In-tree: gates.py line numbers (verify_operator:139, operator_digest:85 with fallback logic at 106-112, hmac.compare_digest:155, g2_approve:378, init_operator_token's repo-path refusal:194-199) all match verbatim; queue.py record_approval:382 has exactly the two-parameter signature claimed, and cli.py's approve subparser (line 773-781) really does accept only task_id/--by/--token, backing acceptance-test-1's 'red because' claim; tests/test_g2_token.py contains exactly 14 tests (not 13 or 15) and every named test (test_deleting_the_working_tree_digest_does_not_disable_g2, test_a_rotated_digest_is_trusted_only_once_committed, etc.) exists, and the g2_enforcement assertions are at exactly lines 66,67,92,180,181,217 as cited. CHANGELOG.md:181-197 confirms verbatim ('The tasks/ tripwire contradicted the engine it guards') that test_no_task_records_are_tracked was retired, and I independently confirmed via grep that no test of that name exists anywhere under tests/ while test_tracked_task_records_are_engine_state_only exists at test_push_boundary.py:248 with the exact docstring quoted — so Open finding 1's handling of the prior lap's disputed baseline is accurate, not swept under the rug. CONTRIBUTING.md:196-198, .env.example:29, .claude/workflows/chimera-build-mode.js:510, BACKLOG.md's Routine/no-connectors line, and TICK_PROTOCOL.md's 'Your job ends at awaiting-signoff' all match verbatim. For the code.claude.com claims I live-fetched both /docs/en/routines and /docs/en/github-actions myself (WebFetch works for that domain) and every quoted string matched word-for-word, including the load-bearing 'the fired prompt is not live user input and can't act as approval or consent for actions during the run', the connectors-attached-by-default/writes-without-asking line, and the Pull-request/Release-only trigger table backing Open finding 6. For docs.github.com claims (blocked here too) I cross-checked every quote against platform-ground's actual report at result-platform-ground.json and found each one — the giving-reviews read-access quote, the branch-protection admin-bypass quote, the Actions create-and-approve default quote, and the REST-reviews field list — present there with the identical confidence caveat (verbatim vs. WebSearch-snippet-only) the artifact assigns it; nothing is upgraded from an unconfirmed source to an asserted fact. I found no fabricated citation, no misquote, and no internal contradiction; the one real evidentiary tension in the run (Open finding 1) is disclosed rather than hidden, and the recommendation's central hedge (two-factor holds only under M1b, which no test can enforce) is stated as a load-bearing qualification rather than buried.

GREP-ANCHOR check across ~30+ citations found essentially everything solid — gates.py:85/106-112/139/155/378/382-384/387 (operator_digest, verify_operator, g2_approve, g2_reject), queue.py:112-124 (LEGAL_TRANSITIONS['awaiting-signoff']=('done','running')), queue.py:354-370 (_enforce_done_gate's three checks), queue.py:382-389 (record_approval signature and awaiting-signoff guard), cli.py:462/468 (cmd_approve/cmd_reject) and cli.py:217/360/392 vs. tick_lock (confirming Open finding 9's claim that approve/reject take no lock), gitio.py:79-87 (commit stages only handed paths), tests/test_g2_token.py (all 14 tests present including the four named, and _signoff_task/_commit_digest/_run at lines 22/42/49 exactly as cited, plus g2_enforcement asserted at exactly lines 66/67/92/180/181/217 as claimed), CHANGELOG.md:181-197 (verbatim match on the retired test_no_task_records_are_tracked description), tests/test_push_boundary.py (confirmed zero hits for that retired test name and test_tracked_task_records_are_engine_state_only at line 248 with the exact 'tasks/ IS tracked, by design' docstring quote), CONTRIBUTING.md:196-198 (Required approvals: 0 / Code Owners instruction verbatim), .env.example:29 and chimera-build-mode.js:510 (both confirmed as claimed), TICK_PROTOCOL.md and BACKLOG.md quotes (all verbatim), and — via a live WebFetch of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines — every quoted fragment attributed to that page matched exactly ('appears as you: commits and pull requests carry your GitHub user', 'can't act as approval or consent for actions during the run', 'visible to anyone who uses the environment', 'always accepted', Claude can use every tool from an included connector..., and the Pull request/Release-only trigger table). Cross-checking the docs.github.com-sourced claims against the on-disk platform-ground report (result-platform-ground.json) also confirmed every attributed quote (read-access-only review, REQUEST_CHANGES definition, REST reviews field list flagged as WebSearch-snippet-only, admin-bypass line, Actions create-and-approve default, community-discussion/changelog hedge) matches that report verbatim. One concrete anchor failed: section 3 item 6 claims the fork-PR-secrets sentence — 'On public repositories, GitHub withholds secrets from runs triggered by fork pull requests, so the review runs only on pull requests from branches in the same repository' — is '(https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-actions, verbatim; already in .github/workflows/claude-review.yml's header)'. I grepped .github/workflows/claude-review.yml for 'withholds secrets' and 'fork pull request' (zero hits) and read the full header block (lines 1-18); the actual line is a paraphrase, 'Fork PRs get no secrets on GitHub, so the review runs for same-repo PRs only' (line 10), not the quoted sentence. The docs.com sentence itself is verbatim (confirmed via platform-ground's report), but the claim that this exact wording is 'already in' the workflow header is false — the file contains a different, shorter paraphrase. This is a real, checkable overclaim in a document whose whole citation-provenance framework depends on that kind of precision, so per the brief's rule ('any failed substantiation -> refuted=true') I default to refuted, though the defect is narrow (it supports background narrative about fork-PR secrets, not any load-bearing claim of the Option B recommendation) and does not touch the core mechanism.

Checked ~16 in-tree and code.claude.com citations line-by-line (gates.py:85,106-112,139,155,194-199,378-391; queue.py:382; CHANGELOG.md:181-197; tests/test_push_boundary.py — confirmed test_no_task_records_are_tracked does NOT exist, only test_tracked_task_records_are_engine_state_only at line 248 with the quoted docstring; CONTRIBUTING.md:196-198; .env.example:29; .claude/workflows/chimera-build-mode.js:510; ADR-011:201-203; the 14 tests and the 6 g2_enforcement line numbers 66/67/92/180/181/217 in tests/test_g2_token.py) plus a direct WebFetch of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines, which verbatim-confirms every load-bearing quote the artifact attributes to it (appears-as-you, fired-prompt-not-consent, env vars visible to anyone who uses the environment, claude/ pushes always accepted, GitHub trigger categories limited to Pull request/Release). All of that is solid. But the artifact's own Open finding 3 admits, and my independent WebSearch for the GitHub REST 'List reviews for a pull request' response schema failed to confirm, that the fields backing models.py's proposed `ReviewEvidence` (user, state, commit_id, submitted_at, html_url at https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/reviews) were never checked against docs.github.com or a real API response — only a WebSearch snippet the researcher itself flagged as unverified. That schema is load-bearing: section 6 commits to those exact field names for the first implementation slice, and Open finding 3 calls this specific gap 'the load-bearing one' still needing confirmation before the model is written. An empirical claim that directly shapes a Pydantic model's fields, without the obvious authoritative source (the REST API reference itself) ever being fetched or independently reproduced, is exactly the missing-source condition this check exists to catch, regardless of how prominently it is disclosed elsewhere in the document.
